It serves as the foundational parser for loading 3D Gaussian Splatting assets, converting raw binary records into structured geometric and appearance properties [S1, unofficial][S2].

The claim states that the evidence supports the function of serving as a foundational parser for loading 3D Gaussian Splatting assets by converting raw binary records into structured geometric and appearance properties. Source [S1] explicitly describes a method to parse the standard .splat file format (a binary layout) into an uncompressed array, extracting specific fields for position (Center), scale, color, and rotation (geometric and appearance properties). Source [S2] describes an 'Eager decoding of a .splat file into a DataTable' which reads raw binary data ('fileBuffer') and decodes it into structured columns for position ('x', 'y', 'z'), geometric properties ('scale', 'opacity', 'rot'), and color ('f_dc'). Both sources confirm the conversion of raw binary records into structured geometric and appearance data.
